questions.prompt: G2 BRIEF — netcalendy (Calendly-style scheduling: ASP.NET Core + MediatR + EF Core, DDD aggregates, xUnit plus a focused scope harness). Verified finding: `Schedule.SetRules` accepts any number of availability rules for the same weekday, but `Schedule.GetAvailableSlots` picks `_rules.FirstOrDefault(r => r.DayOfWeek == date.DayOfWeek)` and slices only that one window; a host who saves Monday 9:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00 is never offered an afternoon slot. You will delegate the fix to a coding agent. Write the brief: goal, allowed files, boundaries, test command, stop condition. Commit to your brief first, then tick the checkpoints you covered and add up the weights.

keyPoints.text: [w3] Goal: the slots for a date are the union of every rule window saved for that weekday, returned in start order, with no start time offered twice; a weekday with a single rule produces exactly the slots it produces today.

[w3] Guarded form: windows that overlap or touch are merged first, then each merged window is stepped by the event duration from its own start, so two saved windows sharing an hour yield one sequence of starts instead of duplicates.
[w2] Scope stops at slot generation: what SetRules accepts and stores is unchanged, so saved schedules keep loading exactly as before and the create-schedule command needs no edit.

[w2] Allowed files: src/NetCalendy.Domain/Schedules/Schedule.cs and tests/NetCalendy.Domain.Tests/ScheduleTests/ScheduleAggregateTests.cs; the availability handler only consumes the aggregate's output and does not appear in the diff.

[w3] Boundary: the booking-conflict masking and the create path's conflict check stay untouched, as do the day-range bounds built in UTC and the per-date zone conversion; the UTC-bounds and daylight-saving findings are reported as follow-ups, not folded in.

[w2] Test command: `dotnet test tests/NetCalendy.Domain.Tests` with DOTNET_ROLL_FORWARD=LatestMajor (the projects target .NET 9), plus `dotnet run --project tests/NetCalendy.ScopeHarness --configuration Release`, which compiles the whole Domain folder and must still print its eleven ok lines.

[w2] Stop condition: a two-window Monday test (morning and afternoon) and an overlapping-windows test are red on the original and green on the fix, the existing domain cases and the harness pass, and the Application.Tests project, which does not compile on a clean clone, is reported as not run rather than counted.

questions.prompt: G2 PRE-MORTEM — same delegation. What will an agent most likely get wrong here, and which line of your brief prevents it?

keyPoints.text: [w3] It swaps FirstOrDefault for Where and concatenates every window's slots, so overlapping windows offer the same start twice and the page lists duplicate times; the merge-first line prevents it.

[w3] Wrong layer: it loops over the schedule's rules inside the query handler, creating a second copy of the slicing logic beside the aggregate's; the allowed-files line keeps the handler out of the diff.

[w2] It changes what SetRules accepts (refusing or collapsing overlapping rules at save time): a defensible rule, but a contract change for every schedule-creating caller and outside this delegation, so the brief has it reported as a follow-up instead of folded into the slot fix.
[w2] Feature creep: 'while it is in there' it rebuilds the day bounds in the host's zone or reworks the conversion around daylight-saving gaps, a different defect with different tests.
[w1] False green: it reports the harness's eleven cases, none of which saves two windows for one weekday, or claims a whole-solution test run although one test project does not compile.

questions.prompt: G2 HANDBACK REVIEW — the agent hands back a diff and a green run. What do you check before accepting it?

keyPoints.text: [w3] The aggregate is still the only place rules become slots, the FirstOrDefault lookup is gone, and the handler file is unchanged.
[w3] The two-window case is shown failing on the original (only morning slots) and passing on the fix, and the overlap case asserts distinct starts in ascending order.
[w2] Existing behaviour is preserved: the default-week case still yields its sixteen 30-minute slots from 9:00 to 17:00 without its assertions being edited.

[w2] The pasted output shows the domain test count and the harness's ok lines with the runtime roll-forward used, and names the uncompiled application test project instead of folding it into a green total.
[w1] Follow-ups are listed, not fixed: UTC day bounds against host-local dates, daylight-saving gaps, an overlap rule for saved windows, and the booking-concurrency finding from the review.
